A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ETF study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and Appendices A–E are readable and support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v3 reports original human annotations, hallucination-detection experiments, NER evaluations and analyses of generated code summaries.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and reports additional hallucination-detection comparisons using several open models.

M1.justification: ETF retains code parsing, summary entity extraction and filtering, entity matching, heuristic sentence retrieval, LLM intent verification and aggregation at one incorrect entity. Appendix D expands documentation of an already explored prompting alternative; it does not introduce a new framework component.

E1.justification: CodeSumEval names the existing dataset rather than introducing new coverage. Both versions use Java CodeXGLUE snippets, summaries from the same seven generators, and the same reported 411 summaries and 9,933 annotated entity-level samples. Additional detector models do not add datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds direct-prompting comparators using Mixtral-8x22B, Llama-3.1-70B, Llama3-8B and Mistral-7Bv3, and replaces Gemini-1.5 with Gemini-2.0 in the main hallucination comparison. GPT4-Omni remains. This substantially expands the evaluated comparison systems; the NER comparator sets in Tables 4–5 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The main evaluation substantially expands ETF's verifier configurations to include four additional open models with different sizes and architectures, alongside the Gemini version replacement. These are added or replaced experimental conditions. Dataset sampling, annotation procedures, aggregation threshold and the decoding settings documented in Appendix B remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a qualitative breakdown of the previously explored prompt-based intent detector's fabricated, altered and omitted sentences. Section 7.2 adds taxonomy-specific error observations, including recursion and overloading confusion. The Changed Entity Form case replaces a Llama3-70B summary with a CodeLlama-7B example while retaining the same failure category.

E5.justification: Both report Cohen's kappa of 0.72 from 4,354 independently double-annotated tuples. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Changed category percentages are result changes, not changes to uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial results, including Direct/ETF instance F1 pairs of 0.45/0.61 for Mixtral and 0.38/0.54 for Llama-3.1-70B. Gemini-1.5 results are replaced by Gemini-2.0 results under a different model condition; GPT4-Omni scores remain unchanged. Figure 3 revises category percentages, including Code Complexity from 52.9% to 52.1%, and Table 3 adds natural-language entity shares. Fabricated-entity rates move to Table 5 unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version adds or revises formal mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs. The working-memory capacity revision from 2–3 to 3–4 objects concerns conceptual motivation, not a formal assumption underlying ETF.

C1.justification: The taxonomy, dataset, ETF and 73% F1 contributions remain. v4 adds explicit claims that unaltered code and naturally occurring hallucinations reflect realistic usage. Its introductory first-of-its-kind approach claim also drops the earlier entity-level qualification.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 expands explanations of taxonomy categories, their overlap and annotation ambiguity, particularly for insufficient knowledge and identifier-name bias. Section 9 newly identifies multiple LLM calls as an obstacle to real-time deployment. Section 5 also revises the working-memory motivation with a new supporting citation.

D1.justification: v4 replaces the planned code/data release statement with a specific repository link and supplies the previously omitted intent-detection prompt in Figure 8. It clarifies that Table 2 uses macro precision, recall and F1, and explicitly documents unaltered source snippets and naturally generated hallucinations. These are documentation and access-information additions.

R1.justification: v4 adds Cowan (2014) for working-memory motivation and Jiang et al.'s Mixtral of Experts reference. The introduction adds positioning around Amazon Q Developer and IBM Watsonx Code Assistant. The substantive related-work discussion otherwise remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 introduces the CodeSumEval name, copyedits prose and spelling, and expands the introduction. Local restructuring merges Section 5.3 into 5.2, inserts Taxonomy Analysis and subdivides Appendix D. Most section organization and existing narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 revises Figure 1 for legibility, expands Table 2, restructures Tables 3 and 5, and adds the Figure 8 prompt box. Code examples and existing prompt boxes are reformatted. These are localized display changes within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The expanded Direct-versus-ETF comparisons better establish how findings depend on the verifier model. Appendix D's failure analysis, explicit macro averaging and repository link also improve documentation. These gains outweigh a localized reporting regression: v4's entity-level discussion quotes instance-level F1 scores of 0.73 and 0.64, although Table 2 gives entity-level scores of 0.61 and 0.60.
